title: MOTOBOUND motocross: visual review and actual Three.js implementation mapping, 2026-10-18

coverage.meaning: All 100 source images were visually reviewed and individually classified; this does not mean 100 separate new features were implemented.

reviewMethod: All 100 images were inspected on labeled contact sheets; the listed nine were also inspected at original resolution. Original observations and supplied source URLs are retained below. Feature keys resolve to shared implementation/path records to avoid repeating the same mapping per image.
interpretation: Reference images guide silhouettes, materials, composition and handling feedback. Gameplay calibration values are not measurements derived from screenshots.
Source URLs and the PS5-available-title designation are supplied-pack provenance. Capture hardware was not independently verified.
Context entries describe depicted vehicles, maps or presentation features that are outside this implementation. Runtime uses original procedural code and existing assets.

worked_soil.summary: Five wandering and interrupted wheel-pass channels replace three uniform lanes, with compacted dark lows, raised pale aggregate, staggered cleat/rake detail, derivative filtering and locally damp roughness.
worked_soil.scope: Normal, color and roughness shading samples the existing soil compaction/depth fields. It does not displace physical terrain or alter collision, course profile or tyre grip.

prepared_earth_scan.summary: Both outdoor motocross and stadium supercross select the resident mineral dry-earth scan for broad macro color and worked-loam fine detail, avoiding enlarged forest-floor needles and roots on prepared track soil.
prepared_earth_scan.scope: Reuses existing photographed earth assets; no new bitmap assets. Physical soil kind, moisture, vertex color and grass-specific fine-detail slots remain authoritative. Non-MX scan selection is retained.

clods_and_dust.summary: The existing motocross particle pass draws seeded irregular dense clod silhouettes and soft billowing dust envelopes, with separate alpha edges and subtle clod form shading.
clods_and_dust.scope: Keeps the existing 2,400-particle capacity, one Points draw, actual loaded-wheel emission, contacts, lifetimes and wetness inputs. Other offroad modes retain their soft-disc map.

helmet_and_goggles.summary: Profiled motocross helmet shells have a real open eye port, recessed liner, integrated projecting chin guard, conformed vents and a narrower peak; smaller curved smoke/iridescent goggles and material tuning restore protected face and shell depth.
helmet_and_goggles.scope: Procedural geometry retains meaningful detail levels and the existing rider contact/IK rig. New eye opening exists at high, mid and far detail; it is not a painted dark rectangle.

moulded_plastics.summary: Radiator shrouds gain a smooth shallow crown and tucked intake profile. Physical plastic materials gain lower clearcoat, fine mould grain and directionally filtered scuff roughness.
moulded_plastics.scope: Uses bounded tessellation and procedural shading in DirtBikeModel; grain/scuff hooks are installed on high/mid plastic materials. Existing livery artwork, exposed frame and mechanical component layout are retained.

knobby_rubber.summary: Tread lugs use three chamfered rings with a narrow worn crown; separate rough motocross rubber material reuses existing rubber grain maps without inheriting the road drainage shader.
knobby_rubber.scope: Lugs remain merged per wheel and preserve the physical tyre contact envelope. Rubber texture ownership stays with shared BikeMaterials, so disposing one LOD does not break another.

selective_mud.summary: Mud combines filtered fine powder film and clumped wet earth with restrained bump relief; per-material exposure keeps helmet, lens, jersey and number-board readability while lower surfaces retain stronger dirt.
selective_mud.scope: Uses existing snapshot dirt/wetness state. The mud shader is shared by existing offroad material users; untagged materials keep exposure 1. It adds no new accumulation physics.

stadium_audience.summary: Lower stadium rows reuse the shared shaped spectator kit; farther seats use analytic human silhouettes. Stable mixed poses, skin/garment zones and muted clothing replace uniform pegs, with simulation-time-driven motion.
stadium_audience.scope: All 14,821 occupied seats remain. Shared crowd.ts/crowd-impostor.ts outputs, stadium bowl, authored structures, chair positions and occupancy random stream are retained. Two audience batches keep the complete stadium at 15 meshes; no new lights.

recoverable_whip.summary: Steering in flight adds bounded bike yaw beneath the rider; release unwinds it. Sport assists the final approach, while Raw preserves greater player authority. Touchdown resolves actual incoming momentum into the rotated tyre axes and records lateral landing speed.
recoverable_whip.scope: Guarded to mx250/mx450 on motocross/supercross. Yaw is bounded to 0.6 rad and 2.2 rad/s. Whipping does not provide lateral airborne force or bonus speed. Only an actually yawed touchdown adds the immediate crossed-landing crash judgement; ordinary slides retain existing tyre-friction recovery. Qualifying jumps with actual yaw and lateral speed above 5.5 m/s can use the existing lowside recovery path. AI ordinarily targets zero whip; takeover unwinds an active player pose.

flight_camera.summary: During sufficiently fast airborne travel, chase framing follows horizontal velocity instead of whipped chassis yaw, preserving a view along the actual flight/landing corridor.
flight_camera.scope: Existing terrain clearance, landing dip, pause/reset behavior and grounded heading remain. The camera does not alter trajectories or authored jump geometry.

flight_feedback.summary: Controls explain steer-to-whip and release-to-square. Snapshot-based HUD shows BRING IT BACK for a sideways flight and WHIP LANDED only after a qualifying clean touchdown settles; crossed landings retain their warning even after slide speed decays.
flight_feedback.scope: Uses existing pose/velocity snapshot channels and a 0.25 s landing settlement window. Feedback adds no stunt score, boost or new game mode; existing rhythm coach and race-control priority remain.

rider_pose.summary: Existing human build, garment construction, hand/foot contacts, IK, inside-leg corner balance and simulation-driven rider posture are retained; helmet geometry/material edits are separately listed.

mechanical_structure.summary: Existing open chassis, fork/spoke/swingarm/engine structure, livery identity, visible chain/sprocket drive and contact dimensions are retained.

suspension_and_pitch.summary: Existing suspension response/droop, throttle/brake air pitch, physical tyre contacts and jump profiles remain; added yaw/landing-alignment behavior is separately listed.

pack_and_lines.summary: Existing racing-line choice, independent AI trajectories, pack spacing and calibrated AI jump solution remain.

authored_environment.summary: Existing venues, terrain envelope, trees, fences, route markers and event structures remain; material and stadium-audience edits are separately listed.

outdoor_audience.summary: Existing outdoor spectators, placements and shared audience kit are retained. Only the stadium audience population/representation is changed in this pass.

lighting_and_contact.summary: Existing world lighting, shadows, atmospheric depth and physical-contact shading remain. New material contrast is not a global exposure/weather-system rewrite.

contact_roost_emission.summary: Existing driven-wheel contact, load/slip emission, dust/clod lifetime and rain inputs remain; shape and opacity treatment are the new rendering work.

current_presentation.summary: Existing garage/menu layouts, racing HUD placement, rhythm targets, assistance selection and race-control hierarchy remain. Explicit whip/landing instruction and feedback are separately listed.

references.observation: Red bike has narrow rim/spoke outlines, bright fork tubes, separate engine castings and a matte boot beside thin colored plastics.
references.recommendedPrinciple: Preserve slender silhouette and sharpen mechanical/material separation; keep detail subordinate to wheel and frame proportions.

references.observation: Low front view separates dark opaque flying clods from soft tan rear-wheel dust; the rider stands with elbows away from the body.
references.recommendedPrinciple: Give heavy clods irregular opaque shapes and retain standing contact-point articulation.

references.observation: Close rear starting pack shows asymmetrical exhausts, large jersey back numbers, deeply separated knobby tread and dark boot recesses.
references.recommendedPrinciple: Keep numbers readable and vary silhouettes/gear instead of tinting the whole rider and machine identically.

references.observation: Helmet shell and fork have concentrated highlights while jersey fabric is matte with shoulder/elbow folds and a black eye opening.
references.recommendedPrinciple: Use roughness and fine textile variation with a dark goggle cavity, keeping clear plastic/metal/fabric response differences.

references.observation: Airborne red bike has open triangular chassis spaces, a long slim swingarm, bent knees and both boots above the pegs.
references.recommendedPrinciple: Keep visible negative space through the frame and stable hands/feet while airborne.

references.observation: Clean airborne profile shows suspension extension, wheels hanging below the chassis and a torso angled independently from the bike.
references.recommendedPrinciple: Retain suspension droop and controlled body weight while developing recoverable air-control expression.

references.observation: Cornering bike follows a dark depressed rut; the inside boot extends forward and small flexible yellow posts mark the outer bank.
references.recommendedPrinciple: Make rut lows darker and irregular while keeping the rider counterweighted and rideable line clear.

references.observation: Narrow bike is partially surrounded by varied grass in front of layered cool-gray cliffs; the foreground has many small occlusion pockets.
references.recommendedPrinciple: Use irregular grass/earth transitions and layered background values rather than additional geometry in the racing lane.
references.context: Cliff and grass composition are environmental context; no new vegetation or cliff system was added.

references.observation: White boots and the lower engine are visibly mud stained under cool roof lights, while the upper jersey remains mostly clean.
references.recommendedPrinciple: Concentrate dirt beneath the rider and on leading/lower surfaces; preserve stadium lighting contrast.

references.observation: Rear airborne bike reveals a dark underside and muddy tire around bright spokes; receding crowd tiers and beams establish arena depth.
references.recommendedPrinciple: Keep chassis occlusion and material breakup, and vary spectator silhouettes without increasing distant scene contrast.

references.observation: White/blue airborne bike has bright fork stanchions, dark protective lowers, thin frame tubes and clinging dirt around the engine and tread.
references.recommendedPrinciple: Separate bare metal, rubber, plastic and dry dirt response in close views.

references.observation: Green bike at the lineup has a white number plate, black tire sidewalls, gray engine casing and small blue/green rims amid staggered riders.
references.recommendedPrinciple: Preserve distinct component colors and subtle machine identity without copying manufacturer graphics.

references.observation: The rear tire kicks a dense dark clod plume behind the bike; nearer wheels frame a clearer central rider.
references.recommendedPrinciple: Make opaque debris originate at actual loaded driven-wheel contact and avoid uniformly soft particle dots.

references.observation: Rear corner view shows one-sided body weight, crumpled jersey fabric, a vivid back number and a broad dark patch at tire contact.
references.recommendedPrinciple: Keep body counterweight, garment variation and grounded tire shading tied to the physical pose.

references.observation: Black/white airborne rider and machine remain legible through light body panels, dark mechanical recesses and one bright fork.
references.recommendedPrinciple: Use value separation among components instead of globally increasing saturation or exposure.

references.observation: Front-facing outdoor rider crosses dappled tree shadows over uneven multitone dirt; spectators and a blue tower remain beyond fences.
references.recommendedPrinciple: Improve local earth/vegetation contrast and readable route edges while maintaining small spectator scale.

references.observation: Front wheel lifts while a thin dust trail spreads low behind the rear wheel; a large red arena wall has simple structural seams.
references.recommendedPrinciple: Keep acceleration dust low at contact and avoid adding high-frequency clutter to large arena architecture.

references.observation: Warm daylight illuminates brown churned soil, bright narrow spokes and fork tubes; the rider has the inside leg extended.
references.recommendedPrinciple: Retain warm dry-earth mineral tones and bright mechanical accents, with nonuniform tire-worn lanes.

references.observation: Close stadium rider is lit against a tall roof window and muted terraces; the dark track foreground shows displaced fine dirt rather than a smooth plane.
references.recommendedPrinciple: Maintain readable subject/background values and refine close soil breakup without excessive gloss.

references.observation: Two front-facing gate riders have dark goggle openings, broad shoulder lines, bent elbows and separate white gloves over orange controls.
references.recommendedPrinciple: Preserve human shoulder/arm silhouettes and material separation around small hand-control contacts.

references.observation: Two neighboring bikes carry riders with different torso angles and different fork travel instead of matching identical poses.
references.recommendedPrinciple: Vary presentation from actual motion state and machine silhouette while preserving physical contact.

references.observation: Two bikes occupy neighboring deep berm lines; the leading rider extends a boot while the following rider keeps a different posture.
references.recommendedPrinciple: Support independent inside/outside line choices and make rut paths visibly irregular.

references.observation: A leading front rider is separated from a pursuing pack by a light dusty haze, visible front-wheel suspension and blue tents behind fences.
references.recommendedPrinciple: Retain staggered pack visibility and keep dust translucent enough to read the next rider.

references.observation: Close lean shows a shiny compacted rut bottom, coarse displaced soil on the bank, scattered clods and dirt on the boot and lower plastic.
references.recommendedPrinciple: Use locally compacted and damp rut surfaces with rough raised earth, and distinguish opaque debris from dust.

references.observation: Rock trail scene has grass patches, horizontal cliff strata, scattered stones and tiny wooden crossings across a broad green hollow.
references.recommendedPrinciple: Use landscape depth and surface contrast as context; this does not imply adding a trials or cliff map.
references.context: Rock/trials venue and wooden crossings are context only; no trials mode or new cliff trail.

references.observation: Two airborne rear views show heavy reddish mud on boots, tires and engine areas, while jerseys preserve their fabric identities.
references.recommendedPrinciple: Concentrate dirt beneath the rider and maintain independently readable lower-body mechanical parts.

references.observation: Riders cross different corner lines with visibly different lean angles; chain/sprocket and swingarm are exposed on the nearer bike.
references.recommendedPrinciple: Add useful air/line expression and retain mechanically correct chain-drive detail.

references.observation: Three front riders crest together with different wheel heights; dark roost sits behind them and the stands form a soft crowd mass.
references.recommendedPrinciple: Keep a varied pack with distinct silhouettes and restrained spectator color noise.

references.observation: Green bike leans across fine sandy tire marks; the rider counterweights it and a long cast shadow confirms its contact and sun direction.
references.recommendedPrinciple: Preserve inside-leg balance, directional soil marks and consistent contact lighting.

references.observation: Two red bikes on broad open dirt differ in posture and wheel load; low dust, fence segments and tall event structures establish scale.
references.recommendedPrinciple: Keep ground contact and pack variation, with low dust that does not hide the next terrain feature.

references.observation: Bike is whipped almost sideways while the rider bends above it; the jump lip, under-engine guard, wheel spokes and landing lane stay visible.
references.recommendedPrinciple: Make bounded aerial style recoverable before touchdown, maintaining intact body-bike contact and landing preview.

references.observation: Rider stands slightly over an airborne bike under warm daylight; floodlight towers and packed stands remain secondary in the composition.
references.recommendedPrinciple: Keep readable airborne posture and varied muted crowd structure in the background.

references.observation: The actual image depicts an ATV on a mountain trail, with tall irregular conifers, layered cliffs and a receding bright mountain skyline.
references.recommendedPrinciple: Apply landscape depth and vegetation variation as context only; do not label this source a motorcycle or an implemented ATV mode.
references.context: The pictured vehicle is an ATV. Mountain/conifer composition is context only; no ATV mode or new mountain venue.

references.observation: Backlit UTV on rippled beach sand casts a long shadow toward the viewer, with sun haze around a pier and distant palms.
references.recommendedPrinciple: Use controlled warm/cool light separation as context; no beach or UTV feature is implied.
references.context: Beach, palms, pier, UTV and sunset presentation are context only; no UTV/beach venue or lighting rewrite.

references.observation: Outdoor race course contains broad elevated berms, many parallel lines, small crowd groups and tents along its upper boundary.
references.recommendedPrinciple: Favor readable lane topology, irregular bank texture and spectators safely beyond the riding envelope.

references.observation: Outdoor pack spreads across several uneven lines, with one bright leading rider and a low brown dust layer between riders.
references.recommendedPrinciple: Keep independently chosen lines and a transparent near-ground dust plume.

references.observation: A forested jump has darker trees behind the rider and spectators/umbrellas behind fence banners above the corner.
references.recommendedPrinciple: Use forest value layering and human scale behind the boundary while preserving clean jump silhouette.
references.context: Forest and outdoor spectator placement are retained context; the new crowd implementation is confined to stadium.ts.

references.observation: Wide starting pack has distinct jersey colors and numbers against a large event board and layered dark stands.
references.recommendedPrinciple: Retain clear starting information and varying rider/spectator silhouettes without overwhelming the track.

references.observation: Tropical panorama gives a readable valley of routes through varied vegetation, with atmospheric distance toward the ocean.
references.recommendedPrinciple: Use layered environmental scale as context; this image does not justify claiming a tropical open world exists.
references.context: Tropical open-world panorama is context only; no tropical venue or open-world scope change.

references.observation: Canyon rider is small against red rock walls, scattered pebbles and distant hazy mesas; foreground soil has fine directional texture.
references.recommendedPrinciple: Borrow scale, tonal depth and irregular ground breakup without adding a canyon course.
references.context: Only irregular dirt/value principles transfer; canyon walls and a canyon venue are context only.

references.observation: Forest trail rider carves around rough rocks, brown ground, irregular bushes and a thin yellow boundary marker.
references.recommendedPrinciple: Keep naturally broken edge transitions and loose dirt response while avoiding new collision obstacles in riding lanes.
references.context: Rocky forest trail dressing remains environmental context; no new obstacles, forest map or collision hazards.

references.observation: Wide outdoor venue has many irregular berm furrows, compressed tire lines, varied conifer heights, tents and crowd pockets outside fencing.
references.recommendedPrinciple: Add broken/crossing prepared rut structure and varied distant human silhouettes while preserving the authored course envelope.

references.observation: Stadium overview shows localized bright wet patches inside a corner, contrasting with dry tan dirt elsewhere and dark multi-tier crowds.
references.recommendedPrinciple: Restrict smoother wet soil to low/compacted patches; retain overall diffuse dirt and subdued stands.

references.observation: Low rear view passes through a narrow trussed holeshot arch; strong tire shadow and coarse grain reveal the slope of the bank.
references.recommendedPrinciple: Keep ground contact strong and route markers physically legible without covering the track.

references.observation: Aerial freestyle area clearly separates metal launch ramps, asphalt approach strips and sculpted dirt landings among sparse shrubs.
references.recommendedPrinciple: Use takeoff/landing readability as a principle; separate freestyle ramps or a new mode are context only.
references.context: Metal launch ramps and freestyle-area layout are context only; no freestyle mode or separate ramp complex.

references.observation: Sculpted dirt bowl has continuous rounded banks, multiple parallel jumps and darker wheel-worn bands through broad light soil.
references.recommendedPrinciple: Keep broad authored jump silhouettes and improve directional macro wear instead of uniformly repeated texture.

references.observation: Forest track has very clear lane-aligned rake bands in the foreground, irregular tree silhouettes and hazy midground terrain.
references.recommendedPrinciple: Preserve useful groomed rhythm but introduce broken continuity, scale filtering and forest depth.

references.observation: Open-roof stadium has densely varied spectators, strong ribbon hierarchy, engineered roof sections and city silhouettes beyond it.
references.recommendedPrinciple: Improve human mass with variation while preserving existing connected architecture and draw budgets.

references.observation: Indoor overview uses structural roof ribs and dark packed tiers to contain a readable tan rhythm course with many distinct jumps.
references.recommendedPrinciple: Keep the course brighter than the stands; improve crowd silhouettes without changing the stadium layout.

references.observation: Aerial winding track has pale compacted lanes, dark worn grooves, grassy islands and long directional marks through differently sized curves.
references.recommendedPrinciple: Break uniform lane shading with broad compacted patches and irregular groove paths consistent with course direction.

references.observation: ATV on narrow forest trail is grounded by nearby shadows, stones, pine branches and patches of grass that change scale with distance.
references.recommendedPrinciple: Use near/far surface and vegetation contrast as context; no ATV feature is implied.
references.context: ATV, mountain forest and local vegetation are context only; no ATV feature or new trail.

references.observation: Outdoor race stretches around a strongly banked wall with crowd lines and tents following the terrain outside its ribbon fence.
references.recommendedPrinciple: Retain banking readability and human scale behind the course boundary.
references.context: Generic banked dirt remains a material reference; the ATV race and additional venue are context only.

references.observation: Low finish-jump view keeps the rider, lip and finish architecture distinct against layered stands rather than one flat background.
references.recommendedPrinciple: Retain a stable landing preview and varied dark crowd silhouettes during dramatic jump framing.

references.observation: Dense launch pack has different wheel heights and gaps; individual clods are dark specks above a pale low dust film.
references.recommendedPrinciple: Keep physical pack variation and differentiate clod opacity from dust softness.

references.observation: Tall outdoor jump is framed by irregular sunlit trees, upper fencing and a dark board; two riders occupy separate flight paths.
references.recommendedPrinciple: Maintain distinct airborne trajectories and clean rider silhouettes against varied vegetation.

references.observation: Rear chase view approaches a crowded bank with multiple dark deep grooves; riders remain staggered enough to anticipate line choice.
references.recommendedPrinciple: Keep track-forward camera preview and retain independent lines with visibly irregular soil channels.

references.observation: Two rear airborne riders flank a long visible landing straight beneath finish structures, with warm haze giving depth.
references.recommendedPrinciple: Keep landing target and horizon available during jumps while allowing controlled bike style.

references.observation: Low side camera shows a compact group leaning into launch; roost traces individual driven wheels instead of a continuous fog wall.
references.recommendedPrinciple: Tie debris to actual tire contacts and maintain rider-to-rider pose differences.

references.observation: Close rear approach shows uneven rut lows with small smooth wet patches, jagged earthen shoulders, long shadows and a visible finish lip.
references.recommendedPrinciple: Give soil locally varying compaction/wetness and preserve lip/landing visibility during camera motion.

references.observation: Airborne motorcycle is silhouetted against layered red mesas under warm sunset light; open space separates rider and terrain.
references.recommendedPrinciple: Use clear airborne framing and lighting context without claiming a desert course.
references.context: Flight framing transfers; desert mesas and sunset are venue/lighting context only.

references.observation: ATV is airborne above a brown track through large snow patches and detailed mountain rock, with a long clear downhill view.
references.recommendedPrinciple: Use landing preview and value separation as context; no snow or ATV feature is implied.
references.context: ATV and snow/mountain venue are context only; no ATV or snow surface implementation.

references.observation: ATV balances over irregular rock under a low sun with autumn trees behind it and visible diagonal suspension geometry.
references.recommendedPrinciple: Use material/lighting contrast as context; this is not evidence for a rock-crawl mechanic.
references.context: ATV rock-crawl and autumn scene are context only; no rock-crawl mechanic.

references.observation: Several riders enter a rising dirt face at different heights, with clear front-wheel lifts and a dark event board behind them.
references.recommendedPrinciple: Retain physical crest response and distinct pack posture instead of matching every bike to one canned jump.

references.observation: Three riders negotiate dark berm waves; one rider extends a foot and a trailing bike is heavily leaned amid uneven rut ridges.
references.recommendedPrinciple: Keep readable recovery/line states and terrain irregularity; the still does not establish a measured crash or heavy roost event.
references.context: Filename crash/congestion wording is not evidence of a measured crash or heavy roost event in this still.

references.observation: Wide pack launch has differing line choices and front-wheel heights across a sequence of visible pale jumps.
references.recommendedPrinciple: Preserve jump rhythm preview and differentiated rider trajectories.

references.observation: Close outdoor corner pack is partially veiled by warm dust, while high-contrast number plates and helmet shapes remain readable.
references.recommendedPrinciple: Keep dust translucent and low, avoiding loss of neighboring-bike visibility.

references.observation: Leading rider crests a dirt rise above another rider, with next bank and sky defining a clear vertical flight corridor.
references.recommendedPrinciple: Retain controlled air pitch and sufficient camera clearance above jump profiles.

references.observation: Two bikes jump close together at different pitch and lean against blue sky, with small clods crossing the foreground.
references.recommendedPrinciple: Allow bounded independent aerial correction and keep debris geometrically small and irregular.

references.observation: Large pack enters red clay with a separate roost plume behind each bike and individually varied spectators beyond the board line.
references.recommendedPrinciple: Maintain readable pack widths and crowd clothing diversity while preserving individual tire emission.

references.observation: Tight start close-up has riders bent forward at different amounts, varying helmet angles, clothing folds and small mechanical highlights.
references.recommendedPrinciple: Keep contact-preserving human posture with different material response on cloth, helmet and machine.

references.observation: Corner pack has strongly different inside/outside lean angles, boots extended on selected riders and spectators with raised arms in the stands.
references.recommendedPrinciple: Preserve line expression and add stable mixed seated/raised-arm crowd cohorts.

references.observation: Rear chase approaching jump shows dark worn groove channels, pale rough shoulders and two leading bikes whipping before a darker stadium skyline.
references.recommendedPrinciple: Prioritize broken close rut shading, recoverable air style and landing-visible chase composition.

references.observation: Wide stadium flight keeps the next ramp visible under the bike while bright roof ribbons and distant obstacles establish depth.
references.recommendedPrinciple: Preserve terrain clearance and landing preview without moving the authored jump geometry.

references.observation: Top-down corner view reveals a dark tire-carved channel, rough displaced soil shoulders and a thin plume behind a leaning bike.
references.recommendedPrinciple: Use close soil compaction variation and actual contact-derived roost.

references.observation: Outdoor pack jumps over bright pale dirt, with distinct bike shadows and tire bands leading toward an ocean horizon.
references.recommendedPrinciple: Keep altitude/landing readable with contact shadows and directional ground wear; location remains context.
references.context: Generic soil/landing readability transfers; ocean venue and altered lighting are context only.

references.observation: Close stadium corner has overlapping but offset bikes, varied torso angles and dark granular roost close to rear tires.
references.recommendedPrinciple: Maintain independent line spacing and opaque small clods that avoid hiding the central rider.

references.observation: Promotional image combines helmeted riders with dark torso gear and reflective goggle openings against vivid graphic branding.
references.recommendedPrinciple: Preserve helmet/gear value hierarchy as context; do not reproduce publisher composition or branding.
references.context: Helmet material/value cues transfer; publisher branding and promotional composition are not reproduced.

references.observation: Garage staging keeps a standing rider separated from an elevated bike stand, transport truck and restrained floor shadows.
references.recommendedPrinciple: Keep rider and bike clearly readable in current presentation; no new garage set is implied.
references.context: Garage staging is presentation context; the existing garage layout is retained.

references.observation: Front start line presents varied riders beneath bright flame columns and thin trusses; ground stays brown and materially diffuse.
